{{nihongo|'''Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine & Iwato Shrine'''|天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine''' (あまてらすおおみかみたかくらじんじゃ) and '''Iwato Shrine''' (いわとじんじゃ) are {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Kyōkōji, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. The two shrines are adjacent, and the boundary within the precincts is not clearly defined; it is possible to pass between their grounds from beside the stone steps of the approach. As a result, to those unfamiliar with the circumstances, it is difficult to notice that they are separate shrines.

Because the two shrines are closely related in origin, they are intentionally described together here rather than on separate pages.

=== Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine ===
[[image:Takakura-Jinja02.jpg|thumb|right|Torii within the precincts of Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine. The stone pillar beside it bears the inscription “Shikinaisha Takamiza Shrine.”]]
Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine is located on the mid-slope of {{ill|Mount Takayasu|Q11669140|qid=Q11669140}} in the southeastern part of {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. In the Jinmyōchō it is recorded as “{{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Takayasu|Q11669131|qid=Q11669131|lt=Takayasu District}} Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine, two seats, ranked for the Monthly and Niiname Festivals, original name {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasugato-no-kami}},” from which it is thought that the “Amaterasu Ōmikami Shrine” and the “Kasugato Shrine” were once separate shrines. In the past, it was called “Shikinaisha Ōsha Takakura Shrine.”

The enshrined deities are {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}} and {{ill|Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi no Ōkami}}. Additionally, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isetsuhiko-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isetsuhime-no-Mikoto}} are also enshrined.

The date of original enshrinement is unknown, but there is a theory that in the 23rd year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} (479), the deity was transferred here from {{ill|Ise Province|Q864166|qid=Q864166}}{{ill|Ujiyoda Shrine|Q17194122|qid=Q17194122|lt=Ujiyamada}}. Judging from the appearance of the main hall enshrined atop bedrock in a mountain ravine, it is also thought to date back to a much earlier era with origins in {{ill|Prehistoric religion|Q1362894|qid=Q1362894|lt=primitive belief}}.

Beside the shrine’s ritual hall is “Shiragohan Falls,” which is said never to run dry even during droughts.

{{-}}

=== Iwato Shrine ===
{{Shrine
|Name=Iwato Shrine
|Location=Kyōkōji 550, Yao City, Osaka Prefecture
|Enshrined deity={{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}
|Shrine rank={{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=Subsidiary shrine}} <small>(Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine)</small>
|Founded=
|Annual festival=
|Rituals=
|image=[[Image:Iwato-Jinja01.jpg|256px]]<br />Iwato Shrine precincts<br><small>From the right side of the stone steps in the back of the photo, one can pass to the precincts of Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine.</small>
|Alternate name=Iwaya Benzaiten}}
Iwato Shrine is located immediately to the west of '''Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine''', and its main hall likewise sits upon bedrock. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}. It is commonly known as “Iwaya Benzaiten” or “Iwatani Benzaiten.” The sacred object is the entire rocky mountain in the area, though previously a carved wooden statue of {{ill|Benzaiten|lt=Benzaiten|Q818468|qid=Q818468|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten}} served as the sacred object.

It is said that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōbō Daishi}}{{ill|Kūkai|Q222227|qid=Q222227}} founded it here after receiving a {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123|lt=revelation}} from the deity while visiting Takakura Shrine. Originally, it enshrined {{ill|Benzaiten|lt=Benzaiten|Q818468|qid=Q818468|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten}}, an Indian river goddess, and thus had a strong {{ill|Buddhism|Q748|qid=Q748}} influence.

From the medieval period onward, the indigenous Japanese water deity {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}} and the faith of the local '''Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine''' underwent {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} (syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism), and she came to be enshrined as the shrine’s deity. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it attracted the devotion of people in Osaka as a deity of prosperity in business.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, following {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} (the separation of Shinto and Buddhism), the {{ill|Benzaiten|lt=Benzaiten|Q818468|qid=Q818468|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten statue}} was moved to the nearby {{ill|Kyōkō-ji|Q11499468|qid=Q11499468}}. Until then, there had been no clear distinction between Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine and Iwato Shrine, but in the Taishō period it was separated as a shrine enshrining {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}, and in the 9th year of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} it became a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=subsidiary shrine within the precincts}} of '''Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine'''.
